dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...Sonnet. You've been ditching work and sneaking out to play with humans more and more often these past few years, haven't you?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Wh—What's the big deal! We can just leave the work to those Moon Envoys anyway, right?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: You've taken a shine to our new master, sisters, and they're willing to send subordinates to share our work, so what choice do I have but to accept?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Besides, you've been having a great time playing around too, Canon! You even participated in a human festival!

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...That was part of my duty. Their high priest called my name. It is only natural that I had to respond to their voices.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Is pretending to be an ordinary human girl and dancing in front of your own statue also one of your duties? That's news to me.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...I wasn't asking you to call my name... Oh, forget it. Since the new Moon Envoy doesn't mind helping Sonnet with her work...

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Zibai. Her name is Zibai. You really should remember people's names.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...Since Zbai has no objections, I have nothing more to say. However, Sonnet, as The Will of the Moon, you must not forget the basic formulae that keep the world running.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Prepare yourself. I will set you some foundational problems on verifying morphological isomorphisms. You are not to go back to the surface until you have solved them all.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Hehe, how mean. You're just like a villain from an earthbound novel trying to drag the runaway princess back to the moon.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...You are the moon! Don't say things like that.
